newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary farmers abandon plans to blockade borders.
newsitem.headline: Hungary farmers abandon plans to blockade borders.

text.p: Farmers protesting against tax rises have abandoned plans to blockade Hungary's border crossings, Hungarian news agency MTI reported on Sunday.
Instead, the farmers' union METESZ, based in the central Hungarian town of Kiskoros, said in a statement sent to the agency they would slow traffic with their tractors for one day on Wednesday.
The Kiskoros farmers have organised nationwide protests for a month against the government's 1997 income and social security tax increases for individual farmers.

Last Monday they issued an ultimatum to the government, threatening to block border crossings and roads to Budapest unless a demand for unconditional tax relief for farmers earning less than 1.5 million forints ($8,500) a year was met.
Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze warned the farmers that police would prevent them from carrying out the threat.

The union's statement attacked the Socialist-led government's agricultural programme, calling it "the ruthlessly exploitative economic policy pursued by the anti-national liberal-Bolshevist government".

"The statement suggests that an opposition political movement with an extremist rhetoric has emerged," Tamas Bauer, of the Alliance of Free Democrats, the junior party in the governing coalition, said.
